overview: Following early-1931 railway accidents, a cross-reference points to Despatch No. 131, while an excerpt describes a San'yo Main Line crash from excessive speed and Railway Minister Egi's Diet defense, citing declining accident rates despite Depression-constrained improvement spending.

people.name: Eugene H. Dooman
people.role: U.S. diplomatic official in Japan; identified as the sender of Despatch No. 131

subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 131 on railway accidents
subfiles.about: The sheet redirects Despatch No. 131 concerning criticism generated by numerous Japanese railway accidents to decimal-file location 894.00 P R/38.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Dooman's 1931 report on criticism from numerous Japanese railway accidents, filed as Despatch No. 131.

subfiles.title: Despatch excerpt on railway accidents and departmental finances
subfiles.about: The excerpt reports criticism of the Railway Department after a fatal San’yō Main Line accident and records Minister Egi’s defense of its safety record and expenditure priorities.
subfiles.summary: Excerpt describes a San'yo Main Line crash killing nine from excessive curve speed; Railway Minister Egi tells the Diet accidents fell to a third of 1924 levels despite Depression-cut revenue limiting improvement spending.

interest: Shows early-1930s Japanese railway accident criticism and the Railway Minister's statistical defense amid Depression budget cuts.
